title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A generative AI system was used to create non-consensual sexual imagery featuring the faces of Dutch public figures, including celebrities, athletes, politicians, and members of the royal family. The deepfake videos were hosted on a platform with millions of monthly users where creators earned money based on views. The system produced content that is illegal in the jurisdiction where it was deployed, yet the platform did not prevent its creation or distribution.

This is a failure of both the generative model and the hosting platform. The model was used to impersonate real people in sexual contexts without consent, a clear case of non-consensual intimate imagery. The platform failed to moderate or remove the illegal content despite its scale and visibility. Catching this would have required either the AI system to refuse the request, the platform to scan uploads for deepfake sexual content, or human review of popular videos.

Whether the AI system operators knew their technology would be used this way, and whether platform moderation was intentionally absent or merely inadequate, is not established by the reporting.

summary:
Multiple Dutch female celebrities are considering filing charges after discovering manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces on an online platform that attracts 13 million monthly visitors. The videos involve numerous Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Interim Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and encouraged victims to report them. Managers and representatives of various victims have confirmed to the news organization that they have filed reports or are considering legal action.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's face is digitally placed onto adult material, is classified as revenge pornography and is therefore illegal. Creators earn money based on video views and are encouraged to remain anonymous on the platform. Legal experts advise victims to file reports, which can lead authorities to shut down websites containing such material. Other options include starting collective lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. A previous case involving television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma resulted in a 39-year-old man receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours of community service.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
